record.paper_title: Open questions in quarkonium and electromagnetic probes
record.original_question: After properly accounting for the normal nuclear effects already present in proton-nucleus collisions, how much of the φ-meson enhancement observed in heavy-ion collisions remains genuinely anomalous?

evidence.quote: We must also keep in mind that there are "normal nuclear effects" at play in low mass dilepton production, such as the increase of the φ/ω cross-section ratio in p-A collisions [18]. How much of the φ enhancement seen in heavy-ion collisions remains "anomalous" after accounting for a correct extrapolation of the p-A observations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the production of φ(1020) mesons in high-energy nuclear collisions. In proton–nucleus (p–A) collisions, ordinary "cold nuclear matter" effects (e.g., nuclear shadowing/anti-shadowing of parton distributions, initial-state multiple scattering, and final-state hadronic absorption) are known to modify φ-meson production relative to elementary proton–proton (p–p) baselines; in particular, the ratio σ(φ)/σ(ω) is observed to grow with the mass number A.

Define the φ nuclear modification factor in nucleus–nucleus (A–A) collisions at center-of-mass energy √s_NN as
  R_{AA}^{φ}(p_T, y; √s_NN) = (1/⟨N_coll⟩) · (d²N_{AA}^{φ}/dp_T dy) / (d²N_{pp}^{φ}/dp_T dy),
and the analogous factor R_{pA}^{φ} for p–A collisions. Let the "expected" φ yield in A–A collisions from a smooth extrapolation of p–A data be the value of R_{AA}^{φ} obtained by composing/scaling the measured R_{pA}^{φ} (e.g., via a Glauber-based folding of cold nuclear matter effects from each colliding nucleus). Define the "anomalous" φ enhancement as
  Δ^{φ}_{anom}(p_T, y; √s_NN) = R_{AA}^{φ,measured} − R_{AA}^{φ,from p-A extrapolation}.

Problem: Quantify Δ^{φ}_{anom} as a function of collision energy √s_NN, centrality (⟨N_coll⟩ or ⟨N_part⟩), transverse momentum p_T, and rapidity y. In particular, determine whether, after a complete and consistent extrapolation of p–A observations (including A-dependence of σ(φ)/σ(ω), shadowing, and absorption) to the A–A geometry, any statistically significant enhancement of φ production in A–A collisions remains, and characterize its magnitude and kinematic dependence.
artifact.category_tag: Quarkonium and dilepton production in heavy-ion collisions
artifact.status_search_result: Reviews of φ-meson production in heavy-ion collisions and dedicated p–Pb measurements (e.g., at the LHC by ALICE) have substantially clarified cold nuclear matter effects, but a definitive, quantitative subtraction of p–A baselines yielding a universally agreed residual "anomalous" φ enhancement across energies, centralities, and kinematics has not been established. The status of the question therefore appears unresolved/unknown in a precise sense.

status_evidence.title: A Review on ϕ Meson Production in Heavy-Ion Collision
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews φ production mechanisms, strangeness enhancement, and nuclear modifications across AGS, SPS, RHIC, and LHC energies.
status_evidence.claim: Comprehensive survey discusses φ enhancement but does not deliver a final extraction of a purely anomalous component after p–A subtraction.

status_evidence.title: Determination of phi meson nuclear modification factors in p–Pb at ALICE
status_evidence.snippet: Systematic p–Pb measurements of φ(1020) production and nuclear modification factor at LHC energies aim to decouple cold nuclear matter effects from final-state effects.
status_evidence.claim: p–A baselines are being measured to disentangle cold nuclear matter from hot-medium effects, indicating the question is still under active investigation.
